title.narrative: Economic policy reform and management and private sector development

description.narrative: Australia supported the Ministry of Public Administration, Home Affairs, Provincial Councils and Local Government (MPCLG) of Sri Lanka by funding The Asia Foundation (TAF) to provide technical assistance to support the ministry to implement essential reforms in line with Sri Lankan government national priorities. The funding was used to provide valuable research and technical expertise on how to make the country’s local governments financially self-sufficient and resilient against economic shocks, such as the 2022 crisis. Australia supported the ministry to develop a roadmap for key reform areas, that: 1. Implement the recommendations of the Public Expenditure Review Committee (PERC) for provincial councils (PCs) and local authorities (LAs); 2. Support the digitisation of financial management and service delivery in LAs; 3. Create necessary legal and policy interventions to support PCs and LA reform; and 4. Reviews the implementation of local government reforms with stakeholders.

title.narrative: Climate adaptation, mitigation, environment and biodiversity

description.narrative: Australia’s Knowledge and Linkages for Inclusive Economy (KLIE) program invested in the establishment of an ocean forecasting system to improve disaster resilience in Sri Lanka. The system, once established, was transferred to Sri Lanka’s National Aquatic Resources Research and Development Agency. The program was a timely response to the New Diamond oil tanker fire and spillage on the East coast and the plastic pollution incident involving the X-Press Pearl cargo ship. The system accurately predicts 5-day ocean forecasts around Sri Lanka. It will contribute to the safety of fisherfolks and other ocean-workers, by predicting tidal surges and high wave events contributing to coastal erosion and will improve coastal management and research. 110 government officials were trained to use the system. The program also built the capacity of 10 government sectors through four training sessions and short courses on oceanography, coastal physical oceanography, ocean hazards, and data analysis.

In Sri Lanka, improving electoral systems are key for strengthening democratic processes. From 2023-2024, Australia supported the Electoral Commission of Sri Lanka (ECSL) by providing technical assistance through the International Foundation for Electoral Systems (IFES). The program helped improve delivery of national and subnational elections by strengthening risk and mitigation practices, fostering effective collaboration with government (divisional and electoral district secretariat offices), and strengthening election operational planning. IFES trained 244 ECSL and government officials, including 52 women, across six districts in both Sinhala and Tamil languages ensuring officials received training in their native language— a prerequisite for inclusive electoral processes. Survey data showed that 84 percent of the ECSL and government participants demonstrated increased knowledge of transparent and inclusive electoral practices. “This training equips us to conduct efficient, unbiased elections through effective planning and risk management. This valuable knowledge will help us perform our election duties more effectively.” (Additional District Secretary, Matale).

In a region of Sri Lanka increasingly affected by unpredictable weather and limited economic opportunities, 50 rural beneficiaries—many of them women—received hands-on training in beekeeping and ayurvedic herbal cultivation through a climate-smart agriculture initiative implemented by EMACE Foundation under Australia’s Direct Aid Program (DAP). ‍ The initiative promoted sustainable farming practices such as organic composting, water conservation, and intercropping to improve soil health, boost biodiversity, and reduce reliance on harmful chemicals. Participants were empowered to build resilient livelihoods while protecting the local ecosystem. To ensure long-term impact, the program provided training in product development and diversification, including branding, packaging, and cost-effective marketing strategies. Beneficiaries learned not only how to grow and harvest, but also to process and sell honey, herbal teas, and oils—transforming small-scale farms into sources of income and food security. ‍ “I never imagined I could earn money while protecting nature! The beehive process helped me earn extra income and grow more fruits and vegetables,” said one participant. ‍ “Learning how to manage costs and sell my products has changed my life,” shared another. ‍ By combining climate-resilient techniques with market-based skills, the program bridged environmental sustainability and economic empowerment, laying the foundation for stronger, self-reliant communities.

The International Foundation for Electoral Systems (IFES) provided funding and technical assistance to the Federation of Sri Lankan Local Government Authorities (FSLGA), a woman-led NGO focused on improving women’s political representation at local government level. Under the Strengthening Governance (SG) program, FSLGA launched the She Leads initiative for women leaders. It provides support to potential candidates in Local Government Authority (LGA) elections and fosters civic engagement in governance processes. FSLGA also rolled out the Male Allies for Leadership Equality (MALE) sensitization program, which engaged 33 men to support women in community and political activities. The program supported FSLGA to equip 83 women under the She Leads program to launch 34 advocacy and outreach initiatives to increase women and marginalized people's political participation. This included establishing young women's forums within five political parties, equipping them for active roles in subnational government politics.

title.narrative: Economic policy reform and management and private sector development

description.narrative: The Strengthening Governance Program (SGP) has initiated impactful steps to ensure that existing social care and protection assistance are effectively directed to the appropriate target groups. TAF supported the Northern Provincial Council (NPC) in developing a Master Plan for a government-run elders’ home in the Northern Province. ‍ The Master Plan addresses the growing demand for elder care services over the next decade, focusing on expanding services at the Kaithady Elders’ Home, which has grown from an initial capacity of 22 residents to over 200. SGP’s ongoing support includes the preparation of an operations manual and business plan to implement the Master Plan through a phased approach, demonstrating the program’s commitment to long-term, sustainable elder care solutions. ‍ TAF also supported the Ministry of Women’s Affairs of the Northern Province in establishing women-centered Social Care Centres aimed at streamlining and integrating decentralized governance systems to deliver welfare services from both central and provincial governments. ‍ This intervention promotes institutional coordination, digital transformation, and operational standardization, and introduces a monitoring mechanism called Mahalir Manbaham, a centralized, women-focused delivery model that aims to consolidate all women-centered services provided by NPC under one roof, improving access to resources for livelihood development, public services, and overall well-being.

The Strengthening Governance Program (SGP), implemented by The Asia Foundation (TAF) with the Department of Social Services (DSS), ensures social care and protection assistance reach appropriate target groups. ‍ TAF supported the Northern Provincial Council (NPC) in developing a Master Plan for a government-run elders’ home, addressing Sri Lanka’s aging population—12.3% of citizens are aged 60 or older, the highest in South Asia. The plan focuses on expanding services at Kaithady Elders’ Home, which grew from 22 to over 200 residents. Approved by NPC, it outlines a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) model to secure funding for a state-of-the-art facility. ‍ SGP continues support through an operations manual and business plan to implement the Master Plan in phases, ensuring sustainable elder care. TAF also assisted the Northern Province’s Ministry of Women’s Affairs in establishing women-centered Social Care Centres to streamline decentralized governance and welfare delivery. This promotes institutional coordination, digital transformation, and operational standardization. ‍ It introduces Mahalir Manbaham (MM), a centralized model consolidating NPC’s women-focused services, improving access to livelihood resources, public services, and well-being. With SGP’s support, a concept note was developed, and service mapping is underway. SGP will help operationalize MM by integrating front- and back-end operations for seamless service delivery
